sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier is most similar to A. wheeleri (= A. floridensis) among the Nearctic species of Amitermes: the mandible base, the mandibular blade and the marginal teeth are larger and more robust in every respect; the soldier is slightly larger and the head capsule more square. The worker can be distinguished from the worker of A. wheeleri only by its larger size and longer enteric valve (EVA).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule orange-yellow in dorsal view; when filled with secretion the frontal gland is pale yellow and occupies about half the area of the head capsule. Frontal gland opening forming a narrow arch at the middle of the frons, densely surrounded by long setae. Labrum conical, sharply delimited from the postclypeus. Mandibles dark reddish brown from the tip of the mandibular blade to the marginal teeth, the base robust, the lateral tubercle weak. Mandibular blade broad beyond the marginal teeth, then evenly narrowed and curved to the apex. Marginal teeth large, nearly triangular, obtuse. Head capsule oval and inflated in lateral view; submentum projecting, parallel to the ventral margin of the head capsule. Dorsal margin of the head capsule with some dozens of long setae, denser around the frontal gland opening. Anterior margin of the frontal gland opening forming a shallow fold on the frons. Anterior lobe of the pronotum slightly longer than the posterior lobe; pronotal margins with long setae. Measurements (mm, maximum—minimum, mean): head width 0.93—1.18 (1.07); pronotum width 0.56—0.70 (0.64); head length (to postclypeus) 1.16—1.49 (1.32); left mandible, inner base of marginal tooth to mandibular margin 0.14—0.19 (0.17); left marginal tooth width to mandibular margin 0.21—0.28 (0.24); left mandible, outer base of marginal tooth to mandibular margin 0.12—0.18 (0.15). 60 heads, 25 nests.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The second proctodeal segment (P2) is very narrow and tubular; its junction with the third proctodeal segment (P3) forms a circular flare. The enteric valve (EVA) has 6 cushions extending the full length of P2; the posterior end of each cushion is an oval patch of pointed scales, the number of scales varying from about 25 to about 8. The posteriormost scale-bearing cushion has a single row of scales extending forwards and dividing into 2—3 rows anteriorly; the remaining cushions lack a single row but end anteriorly in a row or patch of scales. The cushion with the fewest scales is always opposite the cushion with the most. Distinguishable from the worker of A. wheeleri only by its larger size and longer EVA.

note: Adapted from the species-level description in Scheffrahn (2022), original in English; the soldier and worker sections give characters added by the author to the older descriptions of Banks (1920) and Light (1930a); the alate is given as Unknown in the original; measurements are the maximum—minimum and mean of Table 1; synonymy, figure numbers, localities and type-specimen records are not translated.
